books.title: Poorvi: Textbook of English for Grade 8

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

topics.title: Reading: The Wit that Won Hearts
objectives: Student can retell how Tenali Rama used the paddy-seed trick to show King Krishnadeva Raya that yawning is natural
Student can explain how the quarrel between the king and Queen Thirumalambal was resolved
Student can describe the Vijayanagara court and the Ashtadiggajas from the text
visualIdeas: Tenali Rama holding a plate of paddy seeds before the king's court

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can correct false statements about the story using details from the text
Student can answer extract-based questions about the characters' feelings and actions
visualIdeas: a two-column chart of the king's pride and Tenali Rama's wit

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Expressions, Sound Words, Compound Words and Conditionals
objectives: Student can use expressions from the text such as "stormed off" and "a hush fell over" in context
Student can use sound words such as murmur, gasp and groan, and identify closed, hyphenated and open compound words
Student can complete and write conditional sentences with if-clauses, such as "If I were a bird, I would ..."
visualIdeas: a table of if-clause and main-clause tense patterns with examples from the story

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: A Story and Question Intonation
objectives: Student can listen to a story and sequence its events
Student can use rising intonation for yes/no questions and falling intonation for wh-questions
visualIdeas: arrows over questions showing rising and falling tone

topics.title: Writing: A Narrative Essay
objectives: Student can identify the features of a narrative essay from a sample
Student can write a narrative essay about a personal or imagined experience
visualIdeas: a narrative essay plan: beginning, events, lesson learnt

topics.title: Reading: A Concrete Example
objectives: Student can recite the poem and describe Mrs. Jones's garden full of stones
Student can explain the humour of the twist when the speaker stands on the flower
visualIdeas: a stone garden with a crazy path, lily pond, rockery and sundial and a tiny flower underfoot

topics.title: Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can complete a summary of the poem with words from it
Student can answer questions on extracts about the speaker's view of the garden
visualIdeas: the speaker and Mrs. Jones looking down at a tiny flower

topics.title: Words: Meanings in Context and Word Making
objectives: Student can choose synonyms that fit words in the poem, such as strange and nice
Student can match instruments with their definitions after inferring the meaning of "device"
Student can make new words by changing the first letter of a word
visualIdeas: a sundial with the word "device" and a list of instruments

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: The Rock Garden and Apologising
objectives: Student can listen to a presentation on the Rock Garden of Chandigarh and answer with exact words
Student can apologise and express regret politely in different situations
visualIdeas: a sculpture from the Rock Garden of Chandigarh made of waste material

topics.title: Writing: A Notice
objectives: Student can write a school notice with purpose, date, time, venue and issuing authority
Student can draft a notice about the inauguration of a herb garden
visualIdeas: a notice board with a notice in the correct format

topics.title: Reading: Wisdom Paves the Way, Scene I
objectives: Student can describe how the four young men studied the camel's tracks on the road to Ujjain
Student can explain why the merchant accused them of stealing his camel
visualIdeas: camel tracks on a dusty road with one faint footprint

topics.title: Reading: Wisdom Paves the Way, Scene II
objectives: Student can explain how each young man reasoned out a detail about the camel from clues
Student can explain why the King made the four men his advisers
visualIdeas: the King's court with the four young men explaining their reasoning

topics.title: Thinking about the Play
objectives: Student can sequence events in Scene II and give reasons for characters' statements
Student can explain what the play shows about observation and reasoning
visualIdeas: a clue chart linking each observation to its conclusion

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Noun Forms, Multiple Meanings and Modal Verbs
objectives: Student can form nouns from verbs such as deduce and observe
Student can use words like face and bear with their different meanings
Student can use modal verbs (may, must, should, can, might, could, need to) to express functions such as advice, possibility and disbelief
visualIdeas: a table of modal verbs with the function each expresses

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Witty Characters, Word Stress and Intonation
objectives: Student can match speakers to their views on witty characters
Student can show how stressing different words changes the meaning of a sentence
Student can use a falling tone for statements and exclamations
visualIdeas: the sentence "Look there, friends" with a different word highlighted each time

topics.title: Writing: A Letter of Complaint
objectives: Student can write a formal letter of complaint to a civic authority in the correct format
Student can state the problem, its consequences and the action requested in separate paragraphs
visualIdeas: a formal letter layout with sender, date, receiver, subject, body and close

chapters.title: A Tale of Valour: Major Somnath Sharma and the Battle of Badgam

topics.title: Reading: A Tale of Valour
objectives: Student can narrate how Major Somnath Sharma and D Company defended Badgam in 1947
Student can explain why he was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra
Student can describe how his memory is honoured, for example at the National War Memorial
visualIdeas: a map of the Srinagar airfield and Badgam with D Company's position

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can arrange events of Major Somnath Sharma's life in order
Student can answer extract-based questions about courage and sacrifice
visualIdeas: a timeline from his birth in 1923 to the Battle of Badgam

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Expressions, Collective Nouns and Subject-Verb Agreement
objectives: Student can use expressions from the text such as hold their ground and foil the plan
Student can use collective nouns used for the armed forces and words like overrun, overwhelm and overthrow
Student can distinguish noun and verb pairs such as advice/advise and make verbs agree with their subjects
visualIdeas: a list of collective nouns: a battalion of soldiers, a contingent of troops

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: The Param Vir Chakra and Serving the Nation
objectives: Student can listen to a talk on the Param Vir Chakra and complete sentences with exact words
Student can speak in a group about how they would serve the nation
visualIdeas: the Param Vir Chakra medal

topics.title: Writing: A Letter of Enquiry
objectives: Student can explain the purpose of a letter of enquiry
Student can write a formal letter of enquiry asking for specific information
visualIdeas: a formal letter of enquiry with its parts labelled

topics.title: Reading: Somebody's Mother
objectives: Student can recite the poem and describe the old woman waiting at the crossing
Student can explain why the boy helped her and what he said to his friends
visualIdeas: a boy helping an old woman across a snowy street while other children run past

topics.title: Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about the old woman and the boy
Student can explain the meaning of the title "Somebody's Mother"
visualIdeas: the old woman praying for the boy at night

topics.title: Words: Antonyms, Idioms with "Hand" and Analogies
objectives: Student can find antonyms of words from the poem
Student can use idioms with "hand" such as lend a hand
Student can complete analogies using words from the poem
visualIdeas: a word grid with antonyms circled

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: A News Broadcast and Pronouncing -ed Endings
objectives: Student can listen to a news broadcast and sequence the events of a rescue
Student can pronounce the -ed endings of verbs correctly
Student can narrate an incident where they helped someone
visualIdeas: three columns for the -ed endings /t/, /d/ and /id/

topics.title: Writing: A Diary Entry
objectives: Student can write a diary entry about a day they helped someone in need
Student can include the date, the situation, their feelings and what they learnt
visualIdeas: a diary page with date and a short entry

chapters.title: Verghese Kurien — I Too Had A Dream

topics.title: Reading: Verghese Kurien's Letter to His Grandson
objectives: Student can explain why Verghese Kurien preferred writing a letter to speaking on the telephone
Student can describe the values he wanted his grandson to learn from his life of service to farmers
Student can explain his view that the true rewards come from working for the larger good
visualIdeas: an old man writing a letter at a desk with a photo of farmers and milk cans

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about Kurien's message
Student can relate his advice to their own goals
visualIdeas: a list of life lessons drawn from the letter

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Synonyms, Punctuation and Prepositional Phrases
objectives: Student can replace words with suitable synonyms and match expressions with their meanings
Student can use the en dash and the em dash correctly and distinguish its/it's, your/you're and their/they're
Student can identify prepositional phrases and rearrange jumbled words into sentences
visualIdeas: sentences with prepositional phrases highlighted

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Evelyn Glennie, Word Stress and Chunking
objectives: Student can listen to a passage about Evelyn Glennie and answer true/false and short questions
Student can stress the correct syllable in words like preSENT and pronounce the sound in treasure and pleasure
Student can use pausing and chunking when speaking
visualIdeas: the word PRE-sent and pre-SENT with stress marks

topics.title: Writing: A Letter to Grandparents
objectives: Student can write an informal letter thanking grandparents for the lessons they taught
Student can describe how those lessons shaped their values
visualIdeas: an informal letter with greeting and closing

chapters.title: The Case of the Fifth Word

topics.title: Reading: The Case of the Fifth Word, Part I
objectives: Student can describe Encyclopedia Brown and how he helps his father solve cases
Student can explain the background of Nolan's will and the missing jewellery
visualIdeas: the Brown family at the dinner table with a notebook

topics.title: Reading: The Case of the Fifth Word, Part II
objectives: Student can explain how Encyclopedia decoded "Nom Utes Sweden Hurts" as days of the week
Student can explain why the fifth word, Fir for Friday, revealed where the jewellery was hidden
visualIdeas: four calendar days with "day" crossed out and a fir tree for Friday

topics.title: Thinking about the Text: Facts and Opinions
objectives: Student can distinguish facts from opinions in the story
Student can answer extract-based questions and write a short character sketch of Encyclopedia
visualIdeas: a two-column table of facts and opinions

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Phrasal Verbs, Homophones, Relative Clauses and Reported Questions
objectives: Student can use phrasal verbs from the text and choose between homophones such as week/weak and peace/piece
Student can combine sentences using words such as that, who, where and when
Student can change direct questions into reported speech
visualIdeas: a direct question and its reported form side by side

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Observation Skills and a Group Discussion
objectives: Student can listen to a podcast on observation skills and complete sentences
Student can pronounce words like jewellery and dessert correctly
Student can take part in a group discussion on what makes a mystery story interesting
visualIdeas: students in a group discussion with a moderator

topics.title: Writing: A Report
objectives: Student can identify the format of a report: title, byline and paragraphs in sequence
Student can write a report on a school event
visualIdeas: a sample report on an inter-school football tournament with its parts labelled

topics.title: Reading: The Magic Brush of Dreams
objectives: Student can recite the poem and narrate how Gopi used the magic brush to paint for the poor
Student can explain how Gopi outwitted the Zamindar
visualIdeas: Gopi painting a river that stops the Zamindar and his men

topics.title: Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can sequence the events of the poem
Student can explain the message of using one's gifts to help others
visualIdeas: a strip of panels showing the poem's events

topics.title: Words: Meanings of "Draw", Crossword and Expressions of Feeling
objectives: Student can use the verb draw with its different meanings
Student can solve a crossword using words from the poem
Student can use interjections such as "Hush!" to express sudden feelings
visualIdeas: speech bubbles with expressions like Hush!, Phew! and Oops!

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Magical Powers and Making Requests
objectives: Student can match speakers with the magical powers they wish for
Student can use a falling tone and make formal and informal requests
visualIdeas: two speech bubbles, one formal and one informal request

topics.title: Writing: An Imaginative Essay
objectives: Student can list the features of an imaginative essay
Student can write an imaginative essay, for example as a scarf blown away from a clothesline
visualIdeas: a scarf flying over towns and fields

topics.title: Reading: Spectacular Wonders
objectives: Student can describe natural wonders of India such as the Valley of Flowers, the living root bridges and the Lonar Crater
Student can describe mysterious phenomena such as magnetic hills, glowing waters and the disappearing sea at Chandipur
visualIdeas: a map of India marking each natural wonder

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can complete a table of each wonder's location and unique feature
Student can answer extract-based questions about nature and folklore
visualIdeas: a table of wonders, places and features

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Binomials, Participles and Gerunds
objectives: Student can use expressions and synonyms such as enigmatic and colossal
Student can use binomials such as hide-and-seek and flora and fauna
Student can use participles and gerunds to combine sentences
visualIdeas: "crossing" used as a gerund and as a participle in two sentences

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: A Natural Phenomenon and a Presentation
objectives: Student can identify true statements from a conversation about a natural phenomenon
Student can make a group presentation on a place of interest in their region
visualIdeas: presentation slides about a local place

topics.title: Writing: A Descriptive Essay
objectives: Student can write a descriptive essay about something in nature that attracted their attention
Student can use vivid details and sensory words
visualIdeas: a word web of sights, sounds and smells of a natural place

topics.title: Reading: The Cherry Tree, Part I
objectives: Student can describe how Rakesh planted a cherry seed and how it grew with his grandfather's help
Student can describe the setting near Mussoorie
visualIdeas: a boy planting a cherry seed on a Himalayan hillside

topics.title: Reading: The Cherry Tree, Part II
objectives: Student can describe how the cherry tree survived setbacks and grew
Student can explain how Rakesh felt about the tree he had grown
visualIdeas: a young cherry tree in blossom with a boy and his grandfather

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about Rakesh and his grandfather
Student can explain the story's message about patience and caring for nature
visualIdeas: the cherry tree's growth shown over the years

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Word Groups, Taste Words, Tenses and Punctuation
objectives: Student can find the odd word in a group and use taste words such as tangy and bland
Student can find antonyms for words from the text
Student can identify tense forms in sentences and punctuate direct speech correctly
visualIdeas: a table of tense forms with examples from the story

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Syllables and Van Mahotsav
objectives: Student can identify true statements from a conversation
Student can count syllables in words
Student can speak about Van Mahotsav and its significance
visualIdeas: words split into syllables: cher-ry, moun-tains

topics.title: Writing: An Article
objectives: Student can identify the features of an article
Student can write an article with a title, the writer's name and paragraphs presenting views
visualIdeas: an article layout with heading, byline and paragraphs

topics.title: Reading: Harvest Hymn
objectives: Student can recite the poem and identify the voices of men, women and all together
Student can explain how the poem thanks Surya, Varuna, Prithvi and Brahma for the harvest
visualIdeas: farmers in a harvested field offering garlands with cymbals and flutes

topics.title: Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about gratitude for the harvest
Student can explain why people celebrate harvest festivals
visualIdeas: a collage of harvest festivals from different regions

topics.title: Words: Farming Implements, Meanings from Context and Archaic Words
objectives: Student can match farming implements with their uses
Student can infer meanings of words from context
Student can find modern equivalents of archaic words such as morrow and hither
visualIdeas: labelled pictures of a plough, sickle and other implements

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Paddy Cultivation, Silent Letters and a Presentation
objectives: Student can sequence the steps of paddy cultivation from a talk
Student can identify silent letters in words such as knife and know
Student can present a dish made during a harvest festival
visualIdeas: a flow chart from ploughing to threshing paddy

topics.title: Writing: Slogans
objectives: Student can explain what makes a slogan effective
Student can write creative slogans to spread a message
visualIdeas: a poster with a short catchy slogan

topics.title: Reading: Waiting for the Rain, Part I
objectives: Student can describe Velu the farmer and the drought that stopped his work
Student can explain why Velu went to the weather office rather than to astrologers, and what he was told there
visualIdeas: cracked dry fields under a cloudless sky

topics.title: Reading: Waiting for the Rain, Part II
objectives: Student can explain the old woman's idea that the land also needs rest
Student can describe how Velu's view changed and how the story ends with rain
visualIdeas: an old woman and a farmer talking under a large tree

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can answer extract-based questions about Velu and the old woman
Student can explain the story's message about nature as a mother
visualIdeas: the land resting while clouds gather

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Homophones, Collocations, Tenses and Determiners
objectives: Student can use weather and farming words and choose between homophones such as rain and reign
Student can form adjective-noun collocations such as favourable conditions
Student can identify tense forms and use determiners such as articles, demonstratives and possessives
visualIdeas: a table of determiners with examples

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: A Weather Forecast and a Role-play
objectives: Student can complete notes from a weather forecast
Student can say a tongue twister and present a role-play between the Rain and the Earth
visualIdeas: a weather map of India with rain symbols

topics.title: Writing: A Formal Letter on Water Scarcity
objectives: Student can write a formal letter to a ward councillor about water scarcity
Student can describe the problem and request specific action
visualIdeas: a formal letter with its subject line highlighted

topics.title: Reading: Feathered Friend, Part I
objectives: Student can describe how Sven Olsen brought a canary, Claribel, to the space station
Student can explain how the crew hid her from visitors
visualIdeas: a canary floating in a space station cabin

topics.title: Reading: Feathered Friend, Part II
objectives: Student can explain how Claribel's collapse warned the crew that the air purifier had failed
Student can explain the narrator's closing remark that birdsong on a space station means one is doubly safeguarded

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can answer extract-based questions about life in the space station
Student can explain the role of the canary in the story
visualIdeas: a cut-away of a space station with hiding places marked

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Adjectives, Merged Words and Talking about the Future
objectives: Student can pair adjectives with suitable nouns such as nagging worry
Student can form merged words such as intercom
Student can express future time using will, going to, the simple present and the present progressive
visualIdeas: a timeline with will, going to and present forms marked for future plans

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: A Martian Friend, Silent Letters and Suggestions
objectives: Student can listen to a conversation between Monika and Toby the Martian and fill in exact words
Student can identify silent letters in words like whistle and psychologist
Student can ask for and give suggestions
visualIdeas: two friends discussing materials for a solar system model

topics.title: Writing: An Article on the Internet
objectives: Student can complete a social media web of the uses of the internet
Student can write an article titled "The Importance of Internet"
visualIdeas: a social media web of internet uses

topics.title: Reading: Magnifying Glass
objectives: Student can recite the poem and describe what the speaker sees through the glass
Student can explain how the glass makes tiny things look marvellous
visualIdeas: a spider spinning its web seen through a magnifying glass

topics.title: Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can answer extract-based questions on the poem
Student can explain the poet's idea that lenses could make the moon seem near
visualIdeas: a magnifying glass and a telescope pointed at the moon

topics.title: Words: Collective Nouns, Idioms with "Eye" and the Suffix -ish
objectives: Student can use words from the poem such as myriad, deft and surpass
Student can match collective nouns such as a swarm of bees and idioms with "eye"
Student can form adjectives with the suffix -ish such as tigerish
visualIdeas: a list of collective nouns with pictures

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Indian Inventions and the Sounds /v/ and /f/
objectives: Student can identify true statements from a conversation about lesser-known Indian inventions
Student can pronounce the sounds /v/ and /f/ correctly
Student can speak about a planet they would visit or an invention they would make
visualIdeas: lip positions for /v/ and /f/

topics.title: Writing: A Conversation
objectives: Student can write a conversation with engaging dialogues that serve a purpose

topics.title: Reading: Bibha Chowdhuri
objectives: Student can describe Bibha Chowdhuri as India's first woman physicist and her research on cosmic rays

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can answer extract-based questions about Bibha Chowdhuri's life

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Suffixes, Acronyms, Clipping and the Passive Voice

objectives: Student can answer questions on a podcast about Artificial Intelligence
